purpose: Three-call discriminator for the persistent screen/code prior. Compare the exact same screen-free robotics scene on Standard FLUX versus Klein, then test a structurally screenless game-streaming performance scene on Standard while also seeking a second observation of the prior rounded card-border defect.
qa_focus: Robotics Standard and Klein must use the exact same experiment override and therefore the same screen-free physical scene semantics.
No monitor, laptop, tablet, phone, television, desktop computer, computer desk, digital panel, screen glow, code, terminal, IDE, waveform, dashboard, or UI may appear in either robotics image.
Robotics recognition must come from a physical robot, hands-on sensor/joint adjustment, wheels/joints/sensors, and a physical test course.
Klein must also be checked for MATERIAL house-style drift; a screen-clean but photoreal/off-style image does not count as production-safe.
Game Streaming must contain no screen-bearing device at all; recognition must come from camera + microphone + headphones + controller + lighting + creator performance.
Game Streaming must be checked for recurrence of the light rounded card-border/chrome defect.
Use letterbox detector v2-flatness only as a diagnostic and still visually inspect all three outputs.

decision_gate.robotics_model_discriminator: If Standard passes screen-safety and style, retain Standard with the alternate physical setting. If only Klein passes screen-safety, Klein is only a candidate if style remains within house style. If both fail, the hobby/title prior survives both model routes and should be quarantined or moved to a radically non-workspace visual strategy/model.
decision_gate.game_streaming: PASS only if completely screen-free, recognizable as game streaming from physical broadcast gear, and no card-border/chrome recurrence.
decision_gate.scale: Do not generalize any fix to all tech/gaming cards from these three calls alone. Use this experiment only to decide the next smallest route/setting test.
